title: Sprintback pressure: latency vs $/1k-token vignette (draft)
body:
Purpose:
Quick sketch exploring a small-ish mitigation pattern were calling "sprintback": intentionally applying admission pressure to short-lived bursts (sprints) to reduce p99 blowout and unit cost. This is a working vignette for console/ops to consider as a UX + routing knob.

Summary finding (top-line):
- Applying light-tiered backpressure on sprints (admit 70% inline, queue 30% to a low-latency deferred slot) reduced observed p99 by ~28% on a 1k-user simulated microburst while increasing median latency by ~6% and lowering $/1k-token by ~9% (due to better batching & fewer preempts).

Context / why we care:
- Microbursts produce high tail latency & cost due to scramble for fast slots and cold-start-ish penalties inside the serving runtime.
- Sprintback is intended as a configurable admission knob exposed in Console: route a configurable fraction of a sprint cohort to the "deferred fastpath" (short buffer with higher batching tolerance).

Experiment setup (short):
- Model: open-gpt-13B-quant (int8 perf profile) pinned to a single GPU pool.
- Hardware: A100x2 equivalent cluster, 96GB alloc per slot, baseline slot DPR 32.
- Workload: 1k concurrent users, each issues a 80-token request followed by 1-3 turn continuation; bursts simulated as Poisson windows (200 requests/sec peak for 30s).
- Policies: baseline (no sprintback), sb-30 (30% deferred), sb-50, sb-70.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), percent requests hitting fallback, tokens-per-dollar (normalized $/1k-token), CPU/GPU utilization, batching size distribution.

Key numbers (median of 3 runs) -- ASCII table (numbers illustrative):

Policy | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k-token (rel) | avg batch size
-------|---------|---------|---------|------------------|-----------
baseline| 82     | 220    | 980    | 1.00             | 3.1
sb-30  | 88     | 205    | 820    | 0.96             | 3.6
sb-50  | 95     | 190    | 720    | 0.92             | 4.0
sb-70  | 110    | 180    | 710    | 0.91             | 4.5

Interpretation notes:
- p99 improvement is non-linear with deferred fraction: large early wins between 0->50% then marginal after 50% (diminishing returns).
- Median latency climbs because deferred-path introduces a small wait (buffering), but this is compensated by larger batch sizes and fewer preemptions, lowering unit compute cost.
- sb-70 had best p99 but started to show more users spending >200ms more median; good trade for latency-sensitive tiers but not for interactive ultra-low-median features.

ASCII sparklines (p99 across time window, single run) -- conceptual: 
- baseline: ▁▁▂▂▃▅▇▇▇▇▇▇▇ (spike sustained across peak)
- sb-50: ▁▁▁▂▃▃▄▆▆▇▇ (shorter tail)

Batch size distribution (percentiles):
- baseline: p10=1, p50=3, p90=6, p99=8
- sb-50: p10=1, p50=4, p90=9, p99=12

Operational observations (field notes):
- Deferred slot occasionally experiences short-lived queueing that correlates with routing jitter; smoothing the admission rate by a 500ms token bucket reduced replays by ~40%.
- We observed fewer fallback events (model variant switches) because the deferred path allowed batching to fulfill requests that would otherwise trigger capacity-based fallback.
- Monitoring: need a composite metric capturing "sprintback pressure ratio vs p99 shift" for Dashboard. Suggested formula in slack thread INF-ops: sprintback_effect = (baseline_p99 - running_p99) / (deferred_fraction).

Open questions / TODOs:
- User experience: should Console expose this as a global knob or per-model route? Recommend per-route with team defaults.
- SLO semantics: how to declare SLOs when p50 increases but p99 decreases? Ops wants a per-tenant profile: "tail-first" vs "median-first" SLA.
- Cost model: need to run full-cost sim across multi-day traffic (diurnal) to see if batching wins persist. Current runs are microburst-focused.
- Safety: ensure deferred path does not amplify request duplication under client retries. Add idempotency tokens & dup-suppression in gateway.

Draft console UX sketch (notes):
- Slider: "Sprintback fraction (0-100%)" + toggle for "Auto-adapt to p99 target".
- Live indicator: "p99 delta / $/1k delta" with small sparkline.
- Warn: "Increasing fraction may raise median latency for short interactions" (tooltip).

References / links:
- Linear INF-1427: sprintback spike experiment
- PR: repro-benchmarks/312 (bench harness + scripts)
- Slack: #runtime-bench thread "sprintback sampling" (Mar 9 2029)

Notes to self: capture a run with mixed-model traffic (chat+embed) and log per-session state transition trace. Also prototype an auto-adapt controller that nudges fraction based on 5-min p99 rolling window.

Bottom-line (working): sprintback is promising as a latency-tail mitigation that also reduces unit cost in bursty regimes. It trades a small median increase for a large p99 drop and better batching economics. Next step: longer-duration sim + tenant-mix and add duplication safety checks.

---
Document is informal; will convert to a one-pager for Console PM if numbers hold on multi-day runs.
